title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
This page opens a new 'Analysis' section of E506, Euler's exposition of Lagrange's method (Misc. Taurinensia IV, 1766-69). The method treats the separated equation dx/√X = dy/√Y by turning it into a pair of second-order ODEs in an auxiliary 'time' t. Here Euler applies it to the simplest case, X = A+Bx+Cx², Y = A+By+Cy², with the quartic coefficients D, E set to zero. He announces in advance that this particular route requires D = E = 0.

§27: Introduce t with dt held constant, so that dx/dt = √X and dy/dt = √Y. Squaring gives (dx/dt)² = X and (dy/dt)² = Y.

§28: Differentiate, writing dX = X'dx. Then 2·dx·ddx/dt² = X'dx, so 2x'' = X'(x), and likewise 2y'' = Y'(y). Put p = x+y, so 2p'' = X'+Y'. For a general quartic,
X'+Y' = 2B + 2Cp + 3D(x²+y²) + 4E(x³+y³).
This is a function of p alone only if D = E = 0. In that case 2p'' = 2B + 2Cp is an autonomous linear equation in p. Multiplying by dp and integrating gives (dp/dt)² = Δ + 2Bp + Cp², with Δ an integration constant. Hence dp/dt = √(Δ + 2Bp + Cp²).

The next page combines this with dp/dt = √X + √Y. The result is the algebraic integral √X + √Y = √(Δ + 2B(x+y) + C(x+y)²). Rationalised, this becomes Euler's symmetric biquadratic 'canonical' form α + 2β(x+y) + γ(x²+y²) + 2δxy = 0. It is the algebraic addition law for the elementary (log/arcsin) integrals ∫dx/√(quadratic). The page serves as the warm-up case before the elliptic (quartic) case, where Lagrange's method also needs q = x−y.
errors: No mathematical errors. Every step checks: (dx/dt)² = X gives 2x'' = X'; X'+Y' = 2B+2Cp when D = E = 0; the first integral is (p')² = Δ + 2Bp + Cp².
Minor implicit assumption: the branches of the square roots are chosen consistently (dy/dt = +√Y). This is harmless.

ideas.what: Introducing an auxiliary independent variable t so that a separated differential equation becomes a 'mechanical' system x' = √X, y' = √Y, then differentiating to get second-order equations
ideas.modern_name: Lagrange's method / parametrization by a common 'time' (Hamiltonian-flow viewpoint on the addition theorem)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (Misc. Taur. IV, 1766-69); Euler's E506 is the known exposition
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (Acta Acad. Sci. Imp. Petrop. 1778 II, publ. 1781); also discussed in Opera Omnia I.21 commentary

ideas.what: Passing to p = x+y, whose second derivative depends only on p when X is quadratic, giving a first integral in closed form
ideas.modern_name: Energy integral of a linear autonomous ODE; algebraic first integral

ideas.what: Resulting algebraic integral √X+√Y = √(Δ+2Bp+Cp²) for the quadratic case, matching Euler's canonical symmetric biquadratic
ideas.modern_name: Addition theorem for elementary (degenerate elliptic) integrals
ideas.where_published: E251, E252, Institutiones calculi integralis I

deep.surprise_reason: This is a faithful, correct exposition of Lagrange's well-known method in its simplest quadratic case, within a paper whose content is well documented. Nothing new or uncredited appears.
transcription_corrections: Transcription is essentially accurate; 'dx^2/dt^2' denotes (dx)²/dt², i.e. (dx/dt)².
The cubic term in E's contribution should read x³+y³ (the image shows superscript 3, slightly blurred).
